summary: Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, both attested in 2015.
Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Koyasan University, with his post attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Kato is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. As attested in 2026, he serves as a professor at the University of Tokyo and holds an affiliation with the Eastern Institute.
Takako Abe is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She has held teaching posts at Taisho University, serving as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. He served as professor and president (1989–1995) of Ryukoku University and chaired Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008).

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Waseda University, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Matsumoto Fukashi High School, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne. He founded Waseda University, where he served as a lecturer and Dean of the Faculty of Letters (1930).

Takami Inoue works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Inoue studied as a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as a professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami and at Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, later working with Heinz Bechert and lecturing at Bukkyo University (attested 1999).

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor at Shitennoji University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996; 1999–2016).

Takanori Fukita is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017). He held a post at Bukkyo University and served as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010).

Takao Hayashi is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. His academic career includes posts at Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Doshisha University (1986–2015).
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University until 1962. He held professorships at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; emeritus 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) was a Central Asian and Iranian studies historian who studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He held faculty posts at Kanazawa University, Osaka University (1984–2012), Kindai University (2012–2015), Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo Bunko.

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1969–1998) and served as president of the Society for Indian Philosophy and Religion (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler and Lambert Schmithausen. He served as associate professor (~1987–1992) and professor (~1992–2015; attested 2012–2026) at Waseda University.
Takashi Maeda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 1995 and 2006.

Takashi Nakao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Rissho University and the Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, the Society of Japanese Historical Manuscripts, and Rissho University (emeritus professor 1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo. He was appointed associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
